newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's YPF to build water works after leaks.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's YPF to build water works after leaks.

text.p: Argentine oil giant YPF said Tuesday it will dig water wells to restore supplies to a remote eastern town affected by crude spillages.
The town of Rincon de los Sauces, in Neuquen province some 1,300 km (850 miles) east of Buenos Aires, was affected by recent leaks of crude oil into the Colorado river, its main source of water.
The Rio Colorado lines five provinces and crosses through central Argentina from the Andes to the Atlantic.
As many as 300,000 liters of crude oil may have seeped into the river upstream, where the oil wells are located, after recent storms, according to media reports.
YPF said in a press release it has agreed to build wells, an acqueduct to the center of town and a pumping and purification system in Rincon de los Sauces within 240 days.
In the meantime YPF and other oil companies responsible for the crude leakages will continue to provide local residents, schools and hospitals with mineral water.
On Monday, the government signed a pact with the five provincies involved to ensure proper monitoring of oil firms after the damage to ducts.
The companies claimed that before the leaks on February 16 and March 6 they had hired international consultants to carry out a risk study which did not show any major threat.

YPF, Perez Companc, Petrolera San Jorge, Mexpetrol and Oldeval said in ads published in local newspapers last week that the leaks were caused by torrential rains and slides of water and rocks "which are completely abnormal in the area."
